column1: KHAYA PAYROLL (PTY) LTD — CONSOLIDATED RISK REGISTER
POPIA (8 Conditions) + SOC 2 (CC1–CC9, A1)  |  Version 1.0  |  Prepared for portfolio review

column2: Risk Description
No Information Officer registered with the Information Regulator; no formal ownership of POPIA compliance obligations.
column8: CEO handles queries informally on an ad hoc basis.

column2: Over-collection of special personal information (medical/health data) for sick-leave documentation; no minimum-necessary standard defined.
No documented legal basis mapping data categories to POPIA processing conditions (contract necessity, legal obligation, etc.).
No privacy notice or disclosure process provided to client companies to inform employees of data collection purpose and retention period.
No data retention policy; former employee records persist indefinitely with no defined deletion or archival trigger.
No Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) with third-party sub-processors (Intercom, SendGrid, Payment Gateway); further processing risk unmanaged.
No validation step for sensitive data field updates (banking details, ID numbers); mispayments and fraudulent updates may go undetected.
column8: Employees and HR admins update fields via self-service portal with no secondary confirmation.

column2: No Record of Processing Activities (ROPA); employees unaware of data subject rights (access, correction, objection).
Single-factor authentication only (username/password); no MFA, no encryption confirmed on sensitive fields; broad unlogged internal admin access to all client data.
No documented incident response plan or breach notification procedure; no defined internal escalation path or 72-hour notification benchmark.
No defined data subject request process; requests to access, correct, or delete personal information go unmet with no defined owner or timeline.
No security-specific governance structure; no security policy, no assigned security ownership beyond informal CEO involvement.
No anonymous internal reporting channel for suspected security issues; no external responsible disclosure policy or security@ contact point.
No formal, repeatable risk assessment process; risk reviews are reactive and ad hoc rather than proactive and scheduled.
No mechanism to verify that controls are functioning as intended over time; controls could silently decay without detection.
No formally adopted policies or procedures; all assessment recommendations remain unadopted suggestions without CEO sign-off.
No device offboarding procedure; departing staff laptops not consistently returned or wiped; no building access controls.
No automated monitoring or alerting for suspicious activity; no vulnerability scanning; incident response plan untested.
No formal change management process; code pushed to production without peer review, testing, approval, or documented revert plan.
No vendor register or certificate renewal tracking; no business continuity plan, manual payroll fallback, or client communication plan.
No SLA defined with clients; no uptime monitoring; no capacity planning to manage infrastructure growth.
